Stage 01

Pre-Incorporation & Know-Your-Customer

UBO transparency, Apostille authentication chain, official name clearance restricted wordlist, and pre-incorporation statutory fee budget.

UBO Ultimate Beneficial Owner Screening Rules Official Registry Only

>=25% ownership / control

Applicable AML statute: Law 10/2010 of 28 April on the Prevention of Money Laundering and Terrorist Financing, especially Articles 3, 4, 7, 8, 18 and 25; Royal Decree 304/2014 of 5 May approving the implementing regulation of Law 10/2010; Royal Decree 609/2023 of 11 July regulating the Central Register of Beneficial Ownership; Royal Decree 1021/2015 of 13 November on automatic exchange of financial-account information; Law 58/2003 of 17 December, General Tax Law, for tax-identification and information obligations; Royal Legislative Decree 1/2010 of 2 July approving the consolidated text of the Capital Companies Law for ownership, control, management and corporate-record requirements
Registered Agent & Physical Address Licensed Agent Required

A Spanish S.L. must have a registered office in Spain under the Capital Companies Law. A serviced or virtual office may be acceptable where it provides a genuine legally usable address, receives official correspondence, permits reliable access to corporate records and satisfies the notary, Commercial Registry, Tax Agency, bank and payment-service-provider requirements. A mailbox-only arrangement is unsuitable. For a VPN and network-security SaaS business, the office arrangement must be supported by demonstrable management, technical, contractual and data-protection substance. The company should maintain Spanish corporate books, accounting records, tax records, customer and supplier contracts, security policies, incident records and evidence of effective management. GDPR, Law 34/2002 on Information Society Services and Electronic Commerce, consumer rules, cybersecurity obligations and applicable EU digital-services rules must be assessed separately. The activity generally does not require a telecommunications or financial-services license solely because it provides VPN software, but payment processing, telecommunications resale, cryptography exports, critical-infrastructure services and regulated customers may create additional obligations.

✓ Partner licensed company-secretary channels provide local registered address and government mail forwarding.

Stage 02

Statutory Formation & Board Resolutions

Competent registry, governing statute, capital lockup rules, and first board resolution template.

Competent corporate registry

Registro Mercantil Central for name certification and Registro Mercantil Provincial for registration of the incorporation deed; execution is formalized before a Notary Public.

Governing statute

Royal Legislative Decree 1/2010 of 2 July, approving the consolidated text of the Spanish Capital Companies Act (Ley de Sociedades de Capital); Articles 19–23 (incorporation deed and articles of association), Article 58 (registered office), Article 62 (minimum capital), and Chapter V on the administrative body (directors).

Formation / constitutional filings

Escritura pública de constitución (public incorporation deed), filed with the competent Registro Mercantil Provincial; legal personality is acquired upon inscription.

Incorporation processing time

⚡ 22 business days (SOP sum)

Paid-up Capital & Blocked Account Regime No Capital Lockup Account Required

An S.L. must have minimum share capital of EUR 3,000, fully subscribed and paid-up at incorporation; payment must be evidenced by a Spanish bank deposit certificate or a notarial escrow/deposit certificate.

Funding & unlock path: Non-industrial office workspace: fire-safety compliance under local fire codes, including evacuation plan, extinguishers, and emergency lighting; occupational risk prevention under Ley 31/1995 de Prevención de Riesgos Laborales; structural and occupancy safety evidenced by the municipal first-occupation license (licencia de primera ocupación).

Paid-in capital rule: An S.L. must have minimum share capital of EUR 3,000, fully subscribed and paid-up at incorporation; payment must be evidenced by a Spanish bank deposit certificate or a notarial escrow/deposit certificate.

Stage 03

Tax Identity & Indirect Tax

Tax authority e-portal, entity tax classification elections, VAT thresholds, and 0% export documentation chain.

Tax ID Application Infrastructure

Competent tax authority

Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria (AEAT), Spain's national tax and customs authority; electronic portal: Sede Electrónica de la AEAT (https://sede.agenciatributaria.gob.es). All VAT and corporate income tax filings (modelos 036, 200, 202, 303, 349, 390) are submitted exclusively through the AEAT electronic platform using an e-certificate, Cl@ve PIN, or the EU OSS portal for cross-border digital services.

E-government filing portal

For a Spanish SL: after notarizing the incorporation deed and filing it with the Mercantile Registry (Registro Mercantil), the legal representative applies for the provisional NIF at the local AEAT office using modelo 036, attaching the deed, appointment evidence, and directors' identification; the provisional NIF is granted immediately. Once the Mercantile Registry inscription certificate is presented to AEAT, the definitive NIF (NIF definitivo) is issued. Non-resident shareholders require an individual NIE (Número de Identificación de Extranjero). A non-Spanish entity without a Spanish permanent establishment that needs a NIF for Spanish-source activities or VAT refunds must appoint a fiscal representative (representante fiscal) and file modelo 036/037. Alternatively, a non-established EU supplier of B2C digital services (VPN subscriptions) may avoid a direct Spanish NIF by registering in the OSS Union Scheme in its home Member State, while a non-EU supplier registers in the non-Union OSS scheme or obtains a Spanish NIF for refund purposes.

Tax ID type & application path: Entity_Level_Taxation: a Spanish-resident SL is a separate taxpayer fully subject to the Impuesto sobre Sociedades (Ley 27/2014) at the 25% headline rate (15% for qualifying new operational companies) on worldwide income; no pass-through eligibility exists in any form for an SL. Non-resident entities supplying VPN services without a Spanish permanent establishment are taxed by IRNR (Real Decreto Legislativo 5/2004) on Spanish-source income only; PE profits are taxed at generally 25% before treaty relief. Territorial scope for resident entities is therefore global; a Tax_Exempt_Zone regime exists solely through the Canary Islands ZEC special zone (0%–4% income tax and IGIC instead of IVA) and is not applicable to a mainland Spanish SL. — For a Spanish SL: after notarizing the incorporation deed and filing it with the Mercantile Registry (Registro Mercantil), the legal representative applies for the provisional NIF at the local AEAT office using modelo 036, attaching the deed, appointment evidence, and directors' identification; the provisional NIF is granted immediately. Once the Mercantile Registry inscription certificate is presented to AEAT, the definitive NIF (NIF definitivo) is issued. Non-resident shareholders require an individual NIE (Número de Identificación de Extranjero). A non-Spanish entity without a Spanish permanent establishment that needs a NIF for Spanish-source activities or VAT refunds must appoint a fiscal representative (representante fiscal) and file modelo 036/037. Alternatively, a non-established EU supplier of B2C digital services (VPN subscriptions) may avoid a direct Spanish NIF by registering in the OSS Union Scheme in its home Member State, while a non-EU supplier registers in the non-Union OSS scheme or obtains a Spanish NIF for refund purposes.

Default Tax Classification & Elections

Default tax classification

Entity_Level_Taxation: a Spanish-resident SL is a separate taxpayer fully subject to the Impuesto sobre Sociedades (Ley 27/2014) at the 25% headline rate (15% for qualifying new operational companies) on worldwide income; no pass-through eligibility exists in any form for an SL. Non-resident entities supplying VPN services without a Spanish permanent establishment are taxed by IRNR (Real Decreto Legislativo 5/2004) on Spanish-source income only; PE profits are taxed at generally 25% before treaty relief. Territorial scope for resident entities is therefore global; a Tax_Exempt_Zone regime exists solely through the Canary Islands ZEC special zone (0%–4% income tax and IGIC instead of IVA) and is not applicable to a mainland Spanish SL.

Available election forms

Spain does not provide a US-style check-the-box election; the SL is irrebuttably entity-level taxed. Available relevant statutory elections include: (i) EU ATAD hybrid-mismatch neutralization rules (Ley 27/2014 arts. 15 bis, 23, 62) which operate as mandatory adjustments rather than taxpayer elections; (ii) the optional consolidated corporate tax group regime (RAC) for groups controlling 75% or more of a subsidiary; (iii) the election to apply the 15% reduced corporate income tax rate for newly created companies (entidades de nueva creación) carrying on an active economic activity; (iv) the optional VAT cash-accounting regime (criterio de caja) for taxpayers with annual turnover not exceeding EUR 2,000,000; (v) the simplified VAT regime (régimen simplificado) only for listed small-business activities, which does not cover software or VPN services; and (vi) OSS Union/non-Union registration elections for distance selling and B2C digital services.

VAT / GST & 0% Export Zero-Rating

Standard VAT / GST rate

0.21%

Mandatory registration threshold (Nexus)

No general de minimis VAT registration threshold exists in Spain: any person carrying out economic activities in Spanish territory under the place-of-supply rules (Articles 69-70 Ley 37/1992) must register with AEAT (modelo 036) and file VAT from the first euro of taxable turnover. For non-established EU suppliers of distance-sold goods, the intra-EU distance-sales VAT threshold is EUR 10,000; however, B2C digital services (including VPN subscriptions and privacy software) are deemed supplied in the consumer's EU Member State from the first euro with no threshold, requiring OSS registration (Union or non-Union). The optional Spanish cash-accounting VAT regime (criterio de caja) is available only where annual turnover does not exceed EUR 2,000,000; the simplified VAT regime applies only to statutorily listed small activities and does not apply to a VPN SaaS developer.

Export 0% zero-rating conditions

Goods: the 0% (exempt-with-deduction) rate applies under Article 21 Ley 37/1992 to dispatches to non-EU countries (including Canary Islands, Ceuta and Melilla) provided the goods physically leave the EU customs territory within 90 days of the export declaration and the customs export document (DUA) is validated by Spanish Customs. Services: a VPN/privacy-software SaaS is a service, and supplies to non-EU B2B or B2C customers are outside the Spanish territorial scope under Article 69 Ley 37/1992, resulting in effective 0% treatment when the supplier proves the customer's non-EU status (valid non-EU VAT ID; certificate of residence; ISO country code of customer's billing address/IP/intellectual location) and the actual delivery of the service. Intra-EU B2B supplies are reverse-charged to the customer with a valid EU VAT ID; intra-EU B2C digital supplies are taxed in the consumer's Member State under OSS and are never zero-rated. Ancillary services relating to exported goods (Article 21.2) are zero-rated if they directly benefit the exported goods; VPN-only services do not qualify unless contractually ancillary to qualifying exported goods.

  • Customs Export Declaration (DUA - Documento Único Administrativo) validated by Spanish Customs as proof that the goods left EU customs territory
  • Bill of Lading, Air Waybill, or CMR/CIM transport document proving physical export and EU exit
  • Inward Remittance Certificate (or bank SWIFT/MT103 evidence) evidencing collection of the export proceeds within the statutory period

Electronic invoicing is mandatory for all entrepreneurs in B2B transactions under Ley 18/2022 (Crea y Crece) and Real Decreto 1008/2023, which also establishes the VeriFACTU framework: any invoicing, ERP, or point-of-sale software must guarantee invoice integrity and readability through QR-code/Hashv1-Hashv2 chains and must be certified or compliant before the AEAT. Real-time fiscal clearance applies only to taxpayers subject to the Suministro Inmediato de Información (SII): those with turnover exceeding EUR 6,000,000, VAT groups, and taxpayers in special regimes; SII filers must transmit invoice and VAT-book records to AEAT via web services conforming to the AEAT XSD schemas within 8 calendar days of issuance or use (4 calendar days in certain cases involving invoices over EUR 100,000 or specific journal events). For ordinary SMEs, there is no pre-issuance AEAT stamping or transaction-by-transaction clearance; the business must self-assess the applicable 21% rate, determine the correct place of supply, and submit quarterly modelo 303 and annual modelo 390 returns. Non-resident suppliers using OSS file a single quarterly return through the OSS portal covering all EU B2C digital-sales VAT.

AEAT customs and tax inspection units conduct risk-based export audits, cross-checking the DUA against transport bills, bank flows, and EU administrative cooperation records; the exporter bears the burden of proof of export and of collection of proceeds within 180 days. Failure to substantiate the 0% rate leads to ex officio assessment of the full 21% VAT plus statutory late-payment interest (interés de demora), and, under Ley 58/2003, sanctions ranging from 50% to 150% of the unduly deferred amount depending on concealment and recidivism. Incorrect or missing invoicing is separately penalized (surcharges up to 15% of the invoice amount where the invoice is incorrect, and fines under Article 203 LGT). Where the defrauded amount exceeds EUR 120,000, criminal liability applies under Article 305 of the Código Penal, with imprisonment of 1 to 5 years (up to 6 years in aggravated cases) and a fine of one to six times the amount defrauded. Refunds already obtained are retrospectively clawed back with interest, and the four-year tax statute of limitations (extended in cases of fraud or criminal proceedings) allows reopening of prior periods.

Stage 04

Banking & Treasury Architecture

Central-bank FX diagnosis, tier-1 local banks vs offshore digital EMI matrix, and KYC rejection defense guide.

Foreign Exchange Regime & Central Bank Policy

Current-account convertibility

The euro is fully convertible in Spain. As an EU/EMU member, Spain applies the TFEU free movement of capital regime (Articles 63–64 TFEU) and imposes no exchange controls on current or capital account transactions. Profit remittance, dividend distributions, liquidation proceeds, repayment of shareholder loans, and trade settlements are freely transferable to non-residents, subject to statistical rather than permissive declaration to Banco de España where de-minimis thresholds are exceeded. Spanish dividend withholding tax on outbound distributions is 19% for non-residents without treaty protection, reduced under applicable tax treaties and reduced to 0% under the EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive for qualifying EU parent companies holding at least 10% for at least 12 months; documentation of distributable reserves and shareholding qualification is therefore the operative compliance gate.

Export proceeds surrender rules

None. Spain does not impose any statutory timeline, mandatory conversion ratio, or surrender obligation for export proceeds denominated in euros or foreign currencies. Exporters may retain foreign currency indefinitely in foreign or domestic accounts. The only obligation is timely filing of the Bank of Spain statistical declaration for non-resident collections/receipts above the applicable threshold (Law 19/2003 and implementing regulations), which is purely informational and must be reconciled with the underlying export/service invoices.

Central bank supervision: Banco de España (Bank of Spain) is the central bank and the competent foreign-exchange and monetary authority of the Kingdom of Spain. The Ministry of Economy, Trade and Business exercises foreign-investment screening and registration functions through the Foreign Investment Registry (Registro de Inversiones Exteriores) under Law 19/2003, of 4 July, on the legal regime for capital movements and external transactions.

Offshore Digital Bank / EMI Whitelist

Cross-border EMI / Fintech rails Fit: High

Feasibility rating: Conditional-High for EU-passported Electronic Money Institutions and Spanish licensed payment institutions under PSD2, which can lawfully provide Spanish IBANs and cross-border acquiring without a full banking licence. Legal constraint: non-EEA and post-Brexit UK EMIs are not passportable into Spain and cannot offer local Spanish IBAN collection or direct-debit access; their permitted role is limited to non-EEA settlement corridors or as sub-processor payment gateways. Given the VPN/privacy-software profile classified as Medium_Risk_Enhanced, offshore digital EMIs face heightened onboarding friction; viability depends on a demonstrable compliance programme, transaction transparency, and a contractual cascade that anchors final settlement with a tier-1 Spanish bank.

Core KYC Rejection Triggers & Defense Dossier

VPN and digital encryption software flagged as anonymity enabler and matched against a Medium_Risk_Enhanced underwriting tier with apparent mismatch between declared ISIC 6201 activity and actual subscription-based revenue.

Root cause: VPN and digital encryption software flagged as anonymity enabler and matched against a Medium_Risk_Enhanced underwriting tier with apparent mismatch between declared ISIC 6201 activity and actual subscription-based revenue.

Defense evidence: Certified company statutes and deed of incorporation, original Registro Mercantil certificate, commercial business plan evidencing recurring network-security SaaS character, executed subscription terms and privacy policy (RGPD), live merchant identifiers from Stripe and Paymentwall, sample customer invoices, monthly revenue reconciliation reports, LEI certificate, and a written Spanish AML/CFT compliance manual designating a compliance officer.
Non-face-to-face onboarding of foreign shareholders and UBOs resident in high-risk or offshore jurisdictions, or use of international business-company intermediaries in the ownership chain.

Root cause: Non-face-to-face onboarding of foreign shareholders and UBOs resident in high-risk or offshore jurisdictions, or use of international business-company intermediaries in the ownership chain.

Defense evidence: Apostilled passports, certified certificates of tax residence for each shareholder, source-of-wealth declarations supported by bank references, notarised UBO declarations, corporate-chart diagrams with ownership percentages, and board resolutions approving the capital injection and appointing each authorised signatory.
Irregular inbound flows from crypto exchanges, foreign EMIs, or third-party processors that do not match ordinary SaaS ticket sizes and create a layering/structuring hypothesis.

Root cause: Irregular inbound flows from crypto exchanges, foreign EMIs, or third-party processors that do not match ordinary SaaS ticket sizes and create a layering/structuring hypothesis.

Defense evidence: Three to six months of transaction-ledger extracts from Stripe/Paymentwall, daily settlement reports by currency and card brand, MT940 bank statements reconciled to gateway payout files, subscriber KYC records for bulk B2B purchases, the merchant terms and service-level agreements governing each acquiring rail, and a chartered accountant's or auditor's letter evidencing revenue-recognition traceability to distributable reserves.
Rapid withdrawal or outward disbursement of the injected capital shortly after account opening, triggering money-mule or loan-back structuring suspicion.

Root cause: Rapid withdrawal or outward disbursement of the injected capital shortly after account opening, triggering money-mule or loan-back structuring suspicion.

Defense evidence: Notarised shareholder contribution deed evidencing fully-paid capital, documented source of funds, signed board minutes authorising each specific outbound payment, intercompany or vendor contracts supporting the commercial purpose of the disbursement, a treasury cash-flow forecast, and the preliminary Corporate Income Tax model demonstrating tax-recognised expense treatment.

Cross-Border Clearing Corridors & Settlement Fit

Compliant route: equity contribution formalised by notarial deed and registered with the Registro Mercantil; inbound remittance sent via SWIFT MT103 with ISO 20022 purpose code 'EQUI' or 'CNCB' and remittance field 'Aportación al capital social de la SL'; the beneficiary Spanish bank will credit the escrow capital account and, for euro receipts above the Bank of Spain statistical threshold, the transaction must be declared to Banco de España under Law 19/2003. Parallel notification to the Foreign Investment Registry is required within one month for direct investment in Spain. Alternative route: intra-group shareholder loan using purpose code 'INTC' or 'LEND', supported by a signed interest-bearing loan agreement priced at arm's length for transfer pricing and with full migration to equity upon capitalisation.Preferred clearing rails: SEPA Credit Transfer (SCT) for EEA beneficiaries; SWIFT MT103 telegraphic transfer for non-EEA payees in EUR, USD, or GBP with supporting purpose code (e.g., 'TRAD' or 'SVCL') and invoice reference; for large or risk-mitigated procurement, irrevocable documentary letter of credit issued by the Spanish account bank via SWIFT MT700 and governed by ICC UCP600 and ISBP745 with confirmation bank in the beneficiary jurisdiction. Bulk subscription royalties and SaaS licence fees are settled through Stripe/Paymentwall hybrid payout structure, leveraging a Spanish collection account as the ultimate treasury concentration point feeding T2 (RTGS) and correspondent-bank liquidity.Outright deliverable EUR/USD, EUR/GBP, and EUR/CHF foreign exchange forwards executed with the tier-1 account bank under ISDA 2002 FX Definitions or bilateral master FX termsNon-deliverable forwards (NDFs) for restricted or illiquid Latin American currencies (e.g., Argentine peso, Chilean peso, Mexican peso) where the offshore NDF market provides the only transferable hedgeCross-currency interest rate swaps (CIRS) for long-dated intra-group shareholder loans and intercompany funding structuresVanilla European foreign exchange options (EUR call / emerging-market currency put) for tender contracts and subscription pricing in volatile currenciesMoney-market deposits and T2/euro-system liquidity pooling through virtual IBAN structures for group treasury centralisation without creating non-resident banking friction

E-commerce / gateway settlement fit: Feasibility rating: Conditional-High for EU-passported Electronic Money Institutions and Spanish licensed payment institutions under PSD2, which can lawfully provide Spanish IBANs and cross-border acquiring without a full banking licence. Legal constraint: non-EEA and post-Brexit UK EMIs are not passportable into Spain and cannot offer local Spanish IBAN collection or direct-debit access; their permitted role is limited to non-EEA settlement corridors or as sub-processor payment gateways. Given the VPN/privacy-software profile classified as Medium_Risk_Enhanced, offshore digital EMIs face heightened onboarding friction; viability depends on a demonstrable compliance programme, transaction transparency, and a contractual cascade that anchors final settlement with a tier-1 Spanish bank.

Statutory Filing Calendar

Statutory deliverableDeadline window Government feeDelinquency sanctions
Approval and filing of annual accounts Management must prepare accounts within 3 months after financial year-end; shareholders must approve them within 6 months; filing is due within 1 month after approval. $80 USD Registry closure may apply if accounts remain unfiled for 1 year after the filing deadline. ICAC fines generally range from EUR 1,200 to EUR 60,000, with higher limits for larger entities; registry closure restricts further filings.
Legalization of accounting and corporate books Electronic legalization is generally due within 4 months after the financial year-end. $30 USD Late legalization can impair evidentiary value, create inspection and governance risks, and result in administrative or registry-related enforcement; no general annual franchise penalty applies.
Annual beneficial ownership declaration Filed with the annual accounts and reconfirmed annually; changes in ultimate beneficial ownership should be reported through the applicable notarial or registry process without undue delay. $0 USD Inaccurate or outdated beneficial ownership information may cause filing rejection, registry inconsistencies, notarial or banking restrictions, and potential administrative liability under applicable anti-money-laundering rules.
Corporate income tax annual return (Modelo 200) Generally within 25 calendar days following the 6-month period after the end of the tax period; for a calendar-year taxpayer, normally 1 to 25 July. $0 USD Late filing triggers fixed or percentage-based surcharges and, where applicable, late-payment interest and penalties. The filing is tax compliance rather than a Commercial Registry renewal.
